\section{Gaussian Space --- Bobkov --- Noise}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Bobkov.Noise
\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Bobkov --- Noise: Introduction}
Boolean noise preserves probability-valued functions for correlations in the unit interval. Coordinate decompositions express noised restrictions, last derivatives, and their endpoint ranges.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Bobkov --- Noise: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Range preservation by the noise operator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.noiseOp_mem_unitInterval}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseKernel_sum_right, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_eq_kernel_sum, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{3}
For a natural number $n$, suppose $f\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ takes values in
$[0,1]$, and let $0\le\rho\le1$. Then $T_\rho f(x)\in[0,1]$ for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Linearity of the Boolean noise operator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.noiseOp_linear_combination}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_eq_kernel_sum, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{3}
For a natural number $n$, real numbers $\rho,c,d$, and real-valued functions $f,g$ on
$\{0,1\}^n$, the noise operator satisfies $T_\rho(cf+dg)=cT_\rho f+dT_\rho g$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Noise decomposition of a coordinate restriction]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.noiseOp_restrictLast_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.noiseOp_linear_combination, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast_false_eq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast_true_eq, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb{R}$, $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$,
$b\in\{0,1\}$, and $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. Write $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$,
$a_f(x)=\tfrac12(f(x,0)+f(x,1))$, $d_f(x)=\tfrac12(f(x,0)-f(x,1))$, and $\sigma(0)=1$,
$\sigma(1)=-1$. Applying the noise operator on the first $n$ coordinates gives $(T_\rho
f_b)(x)=(T_\rho a_f)(x)+\sigma(b)(T_\rho d_f)(x)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Last derivative of the noise operator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.derivative_last_noise_snoc}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.derivative_last_snoc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_snoc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign_false, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign_true, BooleanAnalysis.derivative, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, let $\rho\in\mathbb R$,
and choose $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ and a bit $b\in\{0,1\}$. The discrete derivative in the last
coordinate of the noise operator applied to $f$, evaluated at the point obtained by
appending $b$ to $x$, equals $\rho$ times the noise operator applied to the
last-coordinate half-difference of $f$, evaluated at $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Restriction after applying noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.restrictLast_noiseOp_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.noiseOp_snoc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in\bbr$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\bbr$. Write
$f_0,f_1$ for its restrictions to the last coordinate, and set $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$ and
$d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$. For either bit $b\in\{0,1\}$, the restriction of the noise operator
applied to $f$ satisfies
\[
(T_\rho f)_b=T_\rho a_f+\sigma(b)\rho T_\rho d_f,
\]
where $\sigma(0)=1$ and $\sigma(1)=-1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Function identity for noised coordinate restrictions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.noiseOp_restrictLast_eq_fun}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.noiseOp_restrictLast_eq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb{R}$, $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$,
and $b\in\{0,1\}$. Write $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, $a_f(x)=\tfrac12(f(x,0)+f(x,1))$,
$d_f(x)=\tfrac12(f(x,0)-f(x,1))$, and let $\sigma(0)=1$, $\sigma(1)=-1$. As functions on
$\{0,1\}^n$, $T_\rho f_b=T_\rho a_f+\sigma(b)T_\rho d_f$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Range of the noised restriction endpoints]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.noise_restriction_endpoints_mem}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.noiseOp_mem_unitInterval, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.noiseOp_restrictLast_eq, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.avgLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.diffLast, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.restrictLast, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign_false, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign_true, BooleanAnalysis.noiseOp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb{R}$ take values in
$[0,1]$. Suppose $0\le\rho\le1$, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. If $a_f$ is the average of the
two restrictions of $f$ to the last coordinate and $d_f$ is their half-difference, then
both $(T_\rho a_f)(x)+(T_\rho d_f)(x)$ and $(T_\rho a_f)(x)-(T_\rho d_f)(x)$ belong to
$[0,1]$.
\end{lemma}
